_transit_doc: Public transport (sim/transit, sim/commands/transit_commands.cpp). The 4.0's numbers, no source behind them yet: how near a click picks a stop, how far from a street a stop can stand, tracks joined, the most a track runs on a road, a metro entrance's reach, vehicles per line; a bus's dwell, at a terminal, the spacing, how far back it starts, at the stop, the street detour and pace away from the view; a train's dwell, speeds, acceleration and braking, the gap, cars and their length; level crossings: where a vehicle waits, when one closes, the room to the stop line.
_doc: Traffic and pedestrians (sim/traffic). style_share: of the cars, the share of each body style in VehicleType order (sedan first), drawn when a car is made (demand.cpp). people_share: of the people the land use puts on the street; at this share the walking window holds at 16:00 about the 1000 walkers it always had, what the simulation step was measured with (61 of them within 150 m of the map's middle; the Roadcraft 4.0 counted 86 in a smaller city). Who walks: ped_child_share (of those out on foot; below the 19.8% under 15 of IBGE Censo 2022, the youngest do not walk the street, 9% measured in the Roadcraft 4.0), ped_elder_share (IBGE Censo 2022: 15.8% aged 60 or more), ped_elder_pace (Bohannon and Andrews 2011: women of 70-79 1.13 m/s, men of 20-29 1.36 m/s), ped_child_pace (1.23 m/s at 7-12 years, 10 m walk test, SPMRJ); ped_rest_fade_s: a quarter of the walk clip, the time to settle into standing. Anti-gridlock (CTB, Lei 9.503/97, art. 45: not even on green does a driver enter a junction where it may have to stop in the way of the cross traffic; a vehicle commits at its line only with room past the junction and the box clear): jam_seconds/release_every_s jammed-junction release, starve_seconds exit claim, detour_after_s detour at a full exit, reconsider_* route reconsideration in a full queue, bpr_gain congestion cost (the Bureau of Public Roads' travel time, Traffic Assignment Manual, 1964, with the load squared), tail_credit_* room a moving tail frees, gov_* fleet governor. Signals (CONTRAN MBST vol. V, 2022): opposite approaches share a stage, and each stage's green is actuated by the vehicles (cap. 7, green extension, optimum cut): a detection section signal_extension_s[lanes - 1] seconds of travel before the stop line (table 8.1: 4,1 / 1,8 / 1,0 / 0,6 / 0,4 s for 1 to 5 lanes, saturation flow 0,5 ucp/s per lane), each vehicle over it asking for that much more green; the minimum green is the largest of the vehicles' safety green signal_safety_green_s (5.14: never under 10 s), the queue between the section and the line signal_lost_start_s + (distance / signal_queue_spacing_m) x 3600 / signal_sat_flow_lane_h (7.3.1, Eq. 8.2: 3 s, 6 m, 1800 ucp/h per lane) and what the walkers it lets cross need: their safety green ped_safety_green_s (4 s), flashing red ped_reaction_s + crossing length / ped_clear_speed (5.7.2: 1,0 s and 1,2 m/s) and all-red ped_all_red_s (at least 1 s); the maximum green shares out the longest cycle signal_cycle_max_s (5.9: 120 s) left after the intergreens (7.3.3: the flows of a fixed plan are not known beforehand, so the stages get equal shares). The far (meso) traffic asks for green as it leaves a signalled lane, a saturation headway at a time. The intergreen after each green (5.7.1, Eq. 6.4-6.5): amber signal_reaction_s + v / (2 signal_decel) at the regulated speed (t_pr 1,0 s, a_ad 3,0 m/s²), at least amber_min_s up to amber_low_kmh, amber_min_mid_s up to amber_mid_kmh and amber_min_high_s above (3, 4 and 5 s), at most amber_max_s (5 s, the rest goes to the all-red); all-red (d2 + signal_vehicle_m) / v, d2 from the stop line past the junction and the far crosswalk, c 5 m, plus signal_ped_red_s (1 s) when walkers cross in the next stage. At the amber the driver stops unless the vehicle cannot be brought to rest safely (table 3.1): it stops when it can as that timing supposes (reaction, then signal_decel); of the others the amber only covers one that reaches the line before it ends, at its speed and braking at its class's b down to what its turn allows, so any other stops too while its class's b_emergency can do it. Pedestrians: trips of ped_trip_min_m..max_m between nodes; they cross arms along the middle of the painted zebra and vehicles stop behind the stop line (both from data/catalog/street_furniture.json crossing), walkers step off only with ped_critical_gap_s to spare and give a vehicle standing ped_courtesy_s its turn; ped_span_reach_m = heavy half width + 0.9 m either side of a lane. Walking speeds (Weidmann, Transporttechnik der Fussgaenger, IVT ETH Zuerich 1993: free speed 1,34 m/s, standard deviation 0,26 m/s): uniform between walk_speed_min and walk_speed_max, the same mean and deviation (1,34 -+ 0,26 x sqrt 3). Crowd (SUMO MSPModel_Striping, sumo.dlr.de/docs/sumo.html pedestrian.striping.*): the footway in ped_stripe_m stripes (stripe-width 0,64 m), a walker's centre at least half a stripe ped_margin_m off its edges (SUMO walks on the middle of its stripe); a body of radius ped_body_m (Fruin, Pedestrian Planning and Design, 1971: body ellipse 18 x 24 in, taken as the circle on its short axis, 0,46 m); a walker looks ped_look_m ahead, takes the stripe with the most room (ped_lateral_cost per metre aside, ped_keep_right_cost per metre off its own track, a better one only ped_stripe_gain_m better and after ped_stripe_hold_s), steps aside at ped_lateral_share of its pace and keeps ped_gap_m plus ped_headway_s behind a body (ped_accel to speed up again). The same stripes everywhere they walk: each walker sees every body near it (walkers in any mode, the street furniture's footprints) remapped into its own way's frame (SUMO's walking areas), on a sidewalk, round a corner (as wide either side of its line as the sidewalk it heads for, closing toward a place it must reach as fast as it steps aside, the leftmost ped_reserve_share up to ped_reserve_max_m left to those coming the other way: SUMO's reserve-oncoming on walking areas) and over a zebra (its right half only); a body moving slower than ped_moving_ms (under a body's width in 4 s) stands, one heading against its own way comes the other way; held up ped_jam_s on a sidewalk or round a corner, ped_jam_crossing_s on a zebra and ped_jam_narrow_s where its way holds one stripe only (SUMO jamtime 300 s, jamtime.crossing 10 s, jamtime.narrow 1 s) it squeezes past walkers (never furniture) at ped_jam_share of its pace (SUMO: a quarter). At a crosswalk the waiting stand on their own right half of the zebra, kerb_wait_gap_m apart within kerb_wait_half_m of its middle, in up to kerb_wait_rows rows back from the kerb (as many as leave a way along the sidewalk), step forward when a place ahead frees and cross from that place. Walkers appear on the sidewalks whose middle lies within ped_window_m of the camera and are taken away past ped_despawn_window_share of it: the 120 m beyond a 600 m window are half the longest segment (tuning road.max_seg_m, 112 m: 56 m) plus the 64 m the camera moves before the window is looked at again (traffic/window.cpp), so no walker is taken away at the edge it was just put on. Read by native/src/api/traffic_loader.cpp into TrafficParams. Distances in metres, times in seconds, speeds in m/s unless the key says km/h. The near and far models' own numbers, the 4.0's with no source behind them yet: demand_*: the tries at a spawn place and a destination, failed searches a step stands, the most cars, the length at which a segment counts fully, a driver's free-speed share (base plus a random span), where along a segment a car starts and ends (shares of its length) and its start speed (a share of its free speed). junction_signal_arms, junction_signal_main_arms: arms, and main-road arms, that make an automatic junction signalled. lc_force_after_s, lc_force_gap_m: a car waiting this long for a lane it must take accepts these gaps. meso_*: the far model's headway after a signal, after a long or middling junction wait (meso_wait_long_s, meso_wait_mid_s) and otherwise; the speed under which a lane's run is not reckoned; the least wait for a green; the retries behind a full queue and behind the drawn queue; bumper to bumper (meso_fit_m: a jammed lane still lets one in every release); a handover's least and free speeds and share; a tail still this near the lane's start blocks the handover, retried after meso_handover_retry_s. ped_spawn_*: a walker's tries at a place and a destination, and its body's scale. vehicle_*: the pad kept behind anything ahead at an emergency stop (vehicle_safe_pad_m, the lab's physicalMotion.ts PHYSICAL_GAP: a hand's breadth, not the driver's preferred gap), the speeds under which a car waits and is stuck, and the share of its free-road pickup an obstacle must leave a car not to hold it (box_hold). Driving (sim/traffic/vehicle_motion.cpp, vehicle_speed.cpp), the lab's sim/drive/operational.ts, sim/vehicles/driver.ts and curvature.ts: each obstacle is driven against by the adaptive cruise control model (Treiber and Kesting, Traffic Flow Dynamics, 2013, 11.3: the improved IDM and the constant-acceleration heuristic, coolness acc_coolness 0.99 as they use), the pedals easing on at jerk_up and braking harder at jerk_down (m/s³), lifted at once under crawl_ms. The driver (drawn when the vehicle is made): a temper from -1 timid to 1 pushy, (u1 + u2 - 1) x driver_aggression_stretch, spreading the class's a, b, b_emergency by 1 + temper x their spread and its headway and standstill gap by 1 - temper x theirs; its wish speed wanders by drift_amp (drift_amp_min plus up to drift_amp_span) at drift_rate rad/s. Bends: the lateral acceleration a driver accepts falls with speed, lateral_accel_max - lateral_accel_fall x v, never under lateral_accel_min (m/s²), times 1 + temper x lateral_aggression_spread and lateral_heavy_share in a bus or truck; the bend is measured every curve_sample_m as the turn over a chord of curve_chord_m either side, within the braking distance plus curve_look_s of travel and curve_look_m. No outside source for the lab's numbers. Indicators (sim/traffic/vehicle_signals.cpp), the lab's sim/vehicleSignals.ts with no outside source: a turn is signalled turn_signal_s of travel, at least turn_signal_min_m, before the stop line and until turn_signal_until of the connector is driven; a lane change while more than lane_change_done_m of it is left, and the lane a driver signals for lc_signal_s (lc_signal_crawl_s for a change its route needs, under lc_crawl_ms) before moving across. The far (meso) traffic's cars on lanes within far_publish_m of the camera are published where they stand, a body and meso_s0_m apart in a queue, and drawn at the far level (the lab's render/densityCars.ts): past the 1500 m micro window a car is a few pixels, and the 4000 m reach is about where one falls under the lab's 1.5 px (a 4.4 m car at 50 degrees of view on 1080 rows). The front wheels steer by the bend of the path measured over steer_chord_m either side (vehicleSignals.ts pathCurvature). A lane change is a path (lane_change_path.cpp, the lab's params.ts and laneChange.ts): the heading eases from lc_heading_slow to lc_heading_fast rad as the speed rises to lc_fast_kmh, the path never shorter than lc_min_time_s of travel nor lc_min_bodies body lengths; a change the route needs takes the most of lc_room_min_m, lc_room_s of travel and its path plus lc_finish_m, and a driver eases off to the speed at which the changes left fit, never under lc_crawl_ms. window_*: the camera moving this far, or this long passing, looks at the near window again; the room a car materialised behind a tail and before a lane's end keeps; its speed (a share of free speed); the walkers' furniture kept within this many windows (walkers live within 1.2).

styles._doc: What changes with a city's regional style (session-rules.md, section 10). drive_side: right only for now, the lanes are laid out for it, and a style that says left is refused at boot. signal_lenses and signal_plan: read by nothing yet.

roadcraft._doc: The 4.0's: right-hand traffic, three lenses, actuated.

brasil._doc: CTB art. 29, I: circulation on the right. CONTRAN MBST vol. V: three lenses, actuated plans (cap. 7).

europa._doc: To fill from the Vienna Convention on Road Traffic (1968), art. 10, and the Convention on Road Signs and Signals; each state chooses its side: the United Kingdom, Ireland, Malta and Cyprus drive on the left and would be styles of their own.

_kerb_doc: Errands at the kerb (kerb_stops.cpp), the 4.0's numbers, no source behind them, but kerb_end_clear_m: CTB art. 182 I forbids stopping within 5 m of the cross street's kerb line, to which a car's length and the crosswalk (the 4.0 kept 30, and on map 0, its lanes 50 m long on average, nobody ever stopped): share of cars setting somebody down (18 % of the 45 % with a passenger), picking somebody up, trucks on a delivery and how long the mate is away; clear of the street's ends, the planning margin, the stretch it needs, where along it, the room ahead; where the door is along the body and out from it, the clear round its swing and on the footway, its seconds to open and shut, to leave or take a seat, the pace to the door, the give-up time, the pause before opening, how far a walker is looked for and called from.
_lorry_doc: Lorries to the docks (sim/traffic/lorry_traffic.cpp, yard.cpp). lorry_radius_m: the rear axle's path at full lock of AASHTO's SU-30 design vehicle (Green Book: centreline radius 38 ft, wheelbase 20 ft: sqrt(38^2 - 20^2) ft). lorry_rear_m: the body's middle ahead of the rear axle of the Volkswagen Delivery 11.180 the truck is drawn after (agents.json truck: 8.485 long, front overhang 1.26, wheelbase 4.6). lorry_plan_work: the units of work (sim/traffic/way_search.h) a tick spends planning a yard, 1 ms of it at the unit's 0.048 µs measured on the planner's bench (tests/core/yard_bench, 2026-11-05): the 4.0's planning under a millisecond a tick (lorryDocks.ts PLAN_BUDGET). The rest are the 4.0's and have no outside source: how far the search reaches, the stop before a gate, the unloading time.
_classes_doc: [a, b, b_emergency, headway T, min gap s0, share of the speed limit, length, half width] per type: sedan, hatch, suv, van, pickup, moto, bus, truck (drivers.ts ARCH, traffic/state.ts), bicycle. The bus and truck drivers and the bicycle's rider: the lab's sim/vehicles/archetypes.ts (a bicycle is not a slow car: it accelerates gently and brakes far worse than anything with four wheels); the bicycle's length and width SUMO's vClass bicycle defaults (1.6, 0.65) and bike_speed_kmh its desiredMaxSpeed 20 km/h. Where a street has no cycle lane a bicycle rides on the edge of the carriageway (CTB art. 58), its middle bike_edge_m from the lane's edge: half the 1,2 m minimum operating width of AASHTO's Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities, 2012.
_zones_doc: Weights by base zone [none, residential, commercial, industrial, mixed] (traffic.ts:938-947; peds ZONE_PULL).
_people_doc: People on foot by kind of place [home, shop, work, civic]. people_kind_m: per 100 m of street at full bustle; people_busy: how busy each kind is at each hour from midnight, a row a kind (the Roadcraft 4.0's day as drawn by hand, with no survey behind it); people_working, people_purchasing: percent of those aged 15 and over at each hour (BLS American Time Use Survey, table A-3; United States data, the default style's), with work_stay_h and errand_stay_h the stays that turn them over; zone_kinds: what each base zone's land is, a row a zone.
